hypothesis: H5 (primary goal): the SOFR - IORB spread distribution in bp. Step 3, a check of the chosen candidate (s3) of #1145. Development tier
target: spread_bps at the scored day, in basis points, as a 23-quantile distribution at each lead h = 1..5 (scoring_protocol.GRID)

models.candidate: (s3) of #1145: sc_s3_robust (repo_model.spread_mr_state_calendar.ARMS[2], the first of S3_TERMS), the H5 candidate, refit walk-forward as declared in #1196 (metadata/s3_terms_1196.json): the seven location terms month_end, quarter_end, tax_date, settlement_coupon, settlement_bill, dom_19_23 and post_month_end_window in standardised units, a Huber fit, ridge 5, direct pairs, every term read at the target day, refit every 21 decision days, the two-year training window and the minimum of 60 pairs of the base model
models.comparator_a: (a): spread_mr_fhs_mad20_f0.5, #941's scaled mean reversion, the base of (s3); it reads no calendar column and carries the provisional register's mark
models.benchmarks: B1, B1' (repo_model.b1_calendar, #960; beside B1 in every table, B1 stays the protocol's benchmark) and B2 of scoring protocol v1 (repo_model.protocol_benchmarks). B1 and B2 carry the provisional register's mark. A decision day that B2 refuses is recorded as missing (listed in `notes.benchmark_missing`), never filled
models.pairs: direct (training_pairs = 'direct'); the estimation routine is decorated with repo_model.one_step_guard.guard_one_step_fit and needs no allow-list entry. No entry is added to one_step_guard.ONE_STEP_ALLOW_LIST
models.walk: the walk starts where #1196's does, on the first decision day with the history the base model needs, and refits every 21 decision days from there, so every refit date before 2026 is #1196's; the days from 2025-12-04 on are walked in addition. The scarcity state is not read: neither (a) nor (s3) has a state term, and every decision's state is recorded as unknown
models.no_new_arm: no arm, term, setting or tuning is added or changed; (s3+state) and (s3+FOMC/IORB) of #1196 are not scored here

scored_days.decision_days: the decision days whose five targets all fall from 2026-01-02 to 2026-09-03 (first target on or after 2026-01-02, fifth target on or before 2026-09-03) and for which every model has a forecast
scored_days.lockbox: the near-blind tier is open (metadata/lockbox.json, GO #151, 5 October 2026); every scored decision day and target day passes lockbox.require_unlocked through ranking's require_scored_days with the last day 2026-09-03; no day after 2026-09-03 is read, and a day after it raises LookAheadError
scored_days.calibration_table_window: the one exception to the first target day, stated by the ruling: #845's table (the first report) is read over the ordinary target days from 2025-12-12 to 2026-09-03, as #845 declared its stretch (metadata/exploration_845.json), from the lead-h forecast of every decision day whose target falls in it. The days 2025-12-12 to 2025-12-31 were already scored by #1196. The same table is also given on the target days of the scored decision days alone (2026-01-02 to 2026-09-03), where the cells of the second window are a subset of the first's
scored_days.seen_before: these days were already seen by #845 and by the #151 final test. This is a check, not evidence for a verdict or a choice

1_calibration_in_the_large.what: #845's table for (s3) and (a): by lead 1 to 5, on ordinary target days (SplitDeclaration.reporting_day_type(target) == 'ordinary'), the cells, the pressure days (distinct target days above +5 bp), the realised share, the mean P(spread > +5 bp) of each model, and the error mean P less the realised share with its level part and its residual-pool part (the decomposition of scripts/calibration_reserve_mgmt_845.py `decompose`: the level part is what moving each cell's law by the mean of outcome less the law's median would remove; the two add to the error exactly)
1_calibration_in_the_large.event: whole basis points, strictly above: data.exceeds_bp(y, 5.0) and smr.exceedance(23 quantiles, 5.0), as #845
1_calibration_in_the_large.interval: 5th and 95th percentile of a stationary bootstrap over the cells of one lead in target-day order, mean block 10, 10,000 draws, seed 1222 (mean P, realised share and the error resampled jointly, as #845)
1_calibration_in_the_large.minimum: fewer than 3 pressure days in a (window, lead) cell: only its counts are tracked and shown (Eleonora's ruling on #710); its figures go to the --withheld file, which is not tracked, and to the pull request body
1_calibration_in_the_large.day_sets: ordinary target days only (#845's headline); the calm-ordinary sensitivity is not repeated

2_coverage.what: the share of (decision day, lead) cells whose outcome falls in the central 50% band (q25 to q75) and the central 90% band (q05 to q95), nominal 0.50 and 0.90, for (s3), (a), B1, B1' and B2, by lead and by target month, and pooled; with the q95 exceedance. Both hit rules of Eleonora's open question #993 are reported: the closed band (q_lo <= y <= q_hi) and the open band, and the exceedance with y > q and y >= q
2_coverage.interval: 90% stationary-bootstrap percentile interval over the cells in date order: mean block 10 for the cells of one lead, mean block 50 cells (5 x 10) for cells of several leads, 2,000 resamples, seed 1222; none for a group of fewer than 20 target days
2_coverage.month: the calendar month of the target day of the cell

measures: grid CRPS (23 levels), by lead and the mean over leads 1..5 (primary)
upper-tail twCRPS, weight 1{z > 0 bp}, by lead and the mean over leads (key secondary)
3_scores.pairs: (s3) against B1, B1', B2 and (a); (a) against B1, B1' and B2
3_scores.paired: skill = mean(d) / mean(S(benchmark)) with d = S(benchmark) - S(candidate), positive favours the candidate; scoring_protocol.paired_tests, the studentized stationary bootstrap (ruling 1), mean block 10 business days, 10,000 draws, seed 1222; two-sided 90% interval, so the lower end is the one-sided 95% bound. Both the skill interval and the studentized interval on mean d (bp) are reported for every tested row
3_scores.reading: a reading is taken from the mean-d bound (Eleonora's ruling on #1009, 20 October 2026): better when the lower end of the 90% interval of mean d is above zero, worse when the upper end is below zero, otherwise undecided; the skill interval's reading is listed beside it where it differs. Lens C's caveat (the lag-10 HAC standard error is understated about 2x after 2020) is stated on the page. A row whose bound was not computed reads 'no reading' with the reason (#1215)
3_scores.splits: pooled over the scored decision days, by lead, by target month, and by target-day type (month_end, quarter_end, tax_date, settlement, fomc_day, iorb_window, dom_19_23, post_month_end_window, ordinary, and calendar_days; the groups overlap) as #1196. The regime split of the other pages has one regime here (2025-26) and is the pooled row. A target day's score is the mean over the leads that forecast it and it belongs to the group of its own date
3_scores.min_days: a group of fewer than 20 days is listed and not tested (the rule of the H5 pages)
3_scores.day_type_intervals: the intervals on the target-day types and on the months are the current method of the H5 pages: the group's own days are passed to paired_tests as one short series. #1221 asks whether that is right and has not been decided (queued as #1228). The page labels every such interval 'current method' and the rows are not read as evidence for a pressure-day type either way; they follow #1221's outcome when it is merged

pressure_day_types: the benchmarks (B2's pools) and the mean-reversion level read the pressure-day types of the month-end turn record in force since #1161 (repo_model.turn_days.IN_FORCE is True), as every scoring entry point on main does, as #1196 did
reading_rules: A figure is a check on days that #845 and the #151 final test had already seen. Nothing here is a verdict and no choice (adopt, drop, retune) is made on it.
A pooled figure is never read without the month and target-day-type splits beside it.
A cell under 3 pressure days has counts only. The upper-tail and P(> +5 bp) splits are thin: 2026 has few pressure days.
Lens C's caveat is stated on the page; the day-type and month intervals are labelled as the current method (#1221 open).
(a), B1 and B2 carry the provisional register's mark; (s3) reads the calendar at the target day on direct pairs and does not.
